title: Review Content Before Changes Get Expensive

slides.headline: Your content review happens too late.
slides.accentText: Move it before the expensive work.

slides.headline: A finished draft makes the angle feel fixed.
slides.body: By the time the editor sees it, changing direction means revisiting work the team has already done.

slides.title: When you review changes what you must redo.
slides.leftBody: An angle change sends the team back through finished copy.
slides.rightBody: Resolve the angle while the work is still an outline.

slides.headline: Agree on the angle before writing.
slides.body: Decide what the post argues before anyone turns that argument into a full draft.

slides.title: Review the outline before designing slides.
items: Check that the outline supports the agreed angle.
Resolve changes before the outline becomes designed slides.
slides.footer: Review direction while changes are still easy.

slides.title: Put alignment before production.
items: Develop the approved outline into copy.
slides.footer: Make editorial decisions before committing to finished assets.

slides.headline: Early review avoids expensive late changes.
slides.body: Revising an outline means less finished work to revisit than changing the angle after writing and design.

slides.headline: Move the review forward.
slides.body: Agree on the angle first. Review the outline next. Then commit to writing and design.
